analysis:
Integration pass over all 15 units. The PR is documentation and version metadata only: CHANGELOG.md retitles the v0.10.3 candidate section as v0.10.4 (head lines 11-171), six or more changelog.d fragments are deleted and folded into it, docs/operations/provider-release.md is rewritten for 0.10.4 preparation, and ProviderCore.swift line 8 bumps the version from 0.10.3 to 0.10.4. No executable authorization, attestation, encryption, key-handling, workflow or protocol code is changed in the supplied evidence. The replayed deleted fragments match the prose summarized in the units, and none contradicts a canonical control.

The prose describes behavior shipped elsewhere in the PR, and that code is not supplied, so its claims are unverified. Source-pass questions to carry forward:
- T-041: delta complete checkpoints (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS). Check in SSDBlockStore and the checkpoint writers that delta files keep HMAC-only tags, AAD binding to an authenticated parent, the 30-minute TTL and cleanup together with the parent file. Nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed tag may be added.
- TB-012/T-059/T-060/A-018: signer verification before an add-on slot is taken, the 10-second line deadline, non-blocking FIFO-refusing reads, and the model-load fence during a hold.
- TB-011/T-053/T-057: idle-only randomized re-registration of a refused connection. It must start a fresh grant and nonce, never reuse stale authorization, and not be remotely triggerable to cause churn.
- TB-002: 30-second WebSocket upgrade timeout, Qwen grammar-constrained JSON, and forced tool_choice advertised via the self-reported tool_constraint_models.
- The prompt_anchor_mismatch quarantine on provider/coordinator skew is an availability and cache-routing matter and platform-owned.

The release runbook keeps its gates: signed tag, exact CodeDirectory registration, metallib and submodule pin checks, and no automatic enablement. The claim that no provider-version floor is needed relies on external platform behavior I cannot see, so I record it as an unverified contract. No concrete regression is established from these documentation-only changes. Deeper review of the code-bearing units is warranted, so I set needs_deeper_review to true.
